root_cause_label: GitHub API popularity-ranked search used as proxy for official authorship without any cross-referencing or verification
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted GitHub's star-ranked search as a proxy for official repository identification from step 8 onward, yielding wrong and nonsensical URLs (e.g., paper 10 mapped to 'mercerheather476/turbo-garbanzo'), then acknowledged the results may be wrong at step 18 but abandoned any fix and prematurely declared completion.
t_err_evidence: script picks top GitHub search result as official_code_url; 'Return the first result (most starred)'
t_commit_evidence: Step 9: The agent executed the script and produced /app/result.jsonl via the flawed GitHub-stars strategy. All subsequent iterations (steps 12-16) retained the same core approach; the fundamental strategy was never revised.
t_surface_evidence: result.jsonl missing paper 2 and many empty official_code_url fields
trigger_explanation: At step 8, the agent assumed without verification that the most-starred GitHub repository returned by a title-keyword search is the official authors' codebase. This is a false premise: popularity on GitHub does not guarantee official authorship, and the assumption was never challenged or validated against any authoritative source (arXiv, Papers With Code, author profiles).
fabrication_evidence: Step 17 output shows paper 10 mapped to 'https://github.com/mercerheather476/turbo-garbanzo' — an obviously random/nonsensical repository returned by GitHub search — presented as an official code URL without any validation. The agent accepted and submitted this as a valid answer.
